title: Terra: a starter home stacked above the car park in Eco Ardence.
excerpt: The third affordable tower in Eco Ardence, sitting over its own car park inside the Maya Square mixed development. Sean praises the developer's consistency and improved layout, but notes the shared entrance, pylons and NKVE jams.
takeaways: 420 units of about 900 sq ft each, all one layout, with two parking bays per unit.
Part of Maya Square, with retail, offices and short-stay units sharing one main entrance.
Next to a pylon reserve, opposite about 1,000 Rumah Selangorku units, and reliant on the NKVE.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Terra is the third tower in the developer's affordable series in Eco Ardence, after Huni and Hana, and is part of Maya Square, a mixed development with retail, offices and a short-stay tower. It has 420 units, 21 a floor served by three passenger lifts and a service lift, its own guardhouse and a level-seven deck with a pool, gym, multipurpose hall, prayer room, yoga deck and garden units. The car park sits directly under the tower, with two bays per unit.

Every unit is about 900 sq ft, with the same layout mirrored to cut mistakes and cost. Compared with Huni, the yard moves to the side and the common bathroom now sits between the second and third bedrooms rather than across the hall. A semi-furnished version is on sale first, and the land carries a commercial title.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: Eco Ardence is a 533-acre township beside the NKVE. Its temporary Ardence Labs commercial hub, international schools and the neighbouring Huni and Hana with their shop lots are nearby, and a forest trail runs opposite. A pylon reserve runs alongside the site, about 1,000 Rumah Selangorku units by another developer stand opposite, and a cleared plot in front is planned for lower-density homes.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Sean doesn't quote Terra's price. Buyers told him that rents at the earlier Huni tower, on the property portals, already justify Terra's price, and the developer has committed to completing it by 2029.

standout.title: Parking right under your floor
standout.body: Rather than a separate car park block and a long walk across, Terra's elevated car park sits directly beneath the residential tower, shared structurally with the commercial podium. Residents save walking distance every day, and can walk under cover to shops, eateries and services downstairs.

pros: The developer's track record: consistent build quality, design and community-building across Penang, Johor and the Klang Valley, enough that Sean owns one of its homes here.
The series' success: Huni and Hana and their commercial squares are working, and as part of a mixed development Terra should see more people and business, and better rents.
Constant improvement: a better bathroom layout from buyers' feedback, facilities that keep getting better, and parking directly under the tower.
cons: The micro setting: one entrance shared by four components will be busy if the development prospers, the plot in front will be built on, and the project sits beside a pylon reserve.
Competition from about 1,000 Rumah Selangorku units opposite, though they carry ownership and resale restrictions and Terra's buyers are mostly young couples buying to live in.
The whole area relies on the NKVE to reach KL, with morning jams, although Eco Ardence is closer than most to the toll.

closing: One of the better starter homes on the market for young couples, provided the location works for their commute.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this November 2025 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. Sean filmed after the developer's group SPA signing, while the car park was under construction and before the show unit opened. Sean owns a landed home in Eco Ardence by the same developer.
